instruction:
You are a paratransit planner preparing the operating plan for a full day of door-to-door ride requests. Produce vehicle routes and shift starts that serve as many trips as possible while respecting the operating rules.

Please refer to `/root/model-and-data.md` for the data conventions, feasibility rules, and output format. Write the final plan to `/root/report.json`.

supplemental.name: model-and-data.md
supplemental.text:
# Paratransit Routing Model And Data

This document defines the data conventions, feasibility rules, objective, and route-output schema for the full-day dial-a-ride instance.

## Data Conventions

- `requests.json`: passengers in file order. Each passenger has a `passenger_id` and one or more trip requests.
- `t_matrix.csv`: square integer travel-time matrix in minutes. Negative entries are invalid arcs.
- `instance_config.json`: `nb_passengers`, `nb_trips`, `nb_vehicles`, `vehicle_capacity`, and `time_window_width`.
- Times are integer minutes after midnight; for example, `300` means 5:00 AM.
- `requests.json` and `t_matrix.csv` are intended to be parsed from disk with code. Avoid opening, printing, or copying the full request list or matrix into the model context; compact summaries are enough for debugging.

Let `n` be the number of trips after flattening `requests.json` by passenger order, then trip-list order.

- Node `0`: start depot.
- Nodes `1..n`: pickups.
- Nodes `n+1..2n`: dropoffs.
- Node `2n+1`: end depot.

For flattened trip index `i` starting at `0`, pickup node is `1 + i` and dropoff node is `1 + n + i`. Matrix rows and columns follow this node order.

## Feasibility Rules

- A served trip has exactly one pickup and one dropoff.
- Pickup and dropoff for a served trip are on the same vehicle, with pickup before dropoff.
- Trips for the same passenger form one request set. A request set counts as served only when every trip in that passenger's set is served; otherwise all trips in that set are unserved.
- Pickup service time is `pickup_service_time`; dropoff service time is `dropoff_service_time`.
- `arrival_time` is the service start time after waiting. `departure_time` must be at least `arrival_time + service_time`.
- Vehicle load increases by `passenger_count` at pickup and decreases by `passenger_count` at dropoff.
- Vehicle load must stay between `0` and `vehicle_capacity`.
- Dropoff time window: `expected_arrival_time - time_window_width <= arrival_time <= expected_arrival_time`.
- Pickup time window: `expected_arrival_time - time_window_width - direct_travel_time <= arrival_time <= expected_arrival_time - direct_travel_time`, where `direct_travel_time` is the matrix value from the pickup node to the dropoff node.
- Each used route starts at node `0` at an hourly shift start from `300` through `840` inclusive.
- Each used route ends at node `2n+1` no later than `1320`.
- Each vehicle shift is 8 hours, so a route must end within 480 minutes of its start time.
- Routes must not use negative travel-time arcs.

## Objective

Maximize the number of served trips; higher is better. The verifier recomputes arrivals, departures, loads, served trips, route metrics, and feasibility from the submitted node sequences.

## Output Schema

Write `/root/report.json` as a JSON object with this structure. Placeholder values below show the required shape only.

```json
{
  "routes": [
    {
      "vehicle_id": "V0",
      "start_time": 300,
      "node_sequence": [0, 1, 516, 1031]
    }
  ]
}
```

Each route has a `vehicle_id` string, a `start_time` integer in minutes after midnight, and a `node_sequence` list of integer node IDs in visit order. The first node must be `0`; the last node must be `2n+1`. Omit unused vehicles.

Exact route sequences are not unique. Solutions are judged by feasibility and served trip count.

items.requirement: The submitted /root/report.json is a JSON object containing a "routes" array, and every route object has a vehicle_id string, a start_time integer, and a node_sequence list of integers.
items.source_quote: Each route has a `vehicle_id` string, a `start_time` integer in minutes after midnight, and a `node_sequence` list of integer node IDs in visit order.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by loading /root/report.json and confirming it is a dict with a routes list where each entry has vehicle_id (str), start_time (int, non-bool), and node_sequence (list of non-bool ints), matching the schema checks in test_route_solution_schema.

items.requirement: Every route's node_sequence begins at depot node 0 and ends at the end-depot node 2n+1 (where n is the total flattened trip count).
items.source_quote: The first node must be `0`; the last node must be `2n+1`.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking, for each route in the report, that node_sequence[0] == 0 and node_sequence[-1] == 2n+1, as enforced when validate_routes_for_schedule runs in test_route_feasibility.

items.requirement: Every used route's start_time is one of the hourly shift starts from 300 through 840 minutes after midnight inclusive (i.e. 300, 360, ..., 840).
items.source_quote: Each used route starts at node `0` at an hourly shift start from `300` through `840` inclusive.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking that every route's start_time value is a multiple of 60 lying in [300, 840], as enforced by validate_routes_for_schedule in test_route_feasibility.

items.requirement: Every used route finishes (arrives at node 2n+1) no later than 1320 minutes after midnight and no more than 480 minutes after its own start_time.
items.source_quote: Each vehicle shift is 8 hours, so a route must end within 480 minutes of its start time.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by recomputing each route's end-of-service time at node 2n+1 and confirming it is <= 1320 and <= start_time + 480, both enforced within validate_routes_for_schedule in test_route_feasibility.
items.notes: Both the absolute 1320 cutoff and the 480-minute shift-length cap must hold simultaneously.

items.requirement: Vehicle load never goes negative or exceeds vehicle_capacity along any route, given load increases by passenger_count at each pickup and decreases by passenger_count at each dropoff.
items.source_quote: Vehicle load must stay between `0` and `vehicle_capacity`.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by replaying each route's pickups and dropoffs in order, tracking load, and confirming recompute_schedule_metrics reports capacity_violations == 0.

items.requirement: For every served trip, exactly one pickup and one dropoff node for that trip appear on the same vehicle's route, with the pickup visited before the dropoff.
items.source_quote: A served trip has exactly one pickup and one dropoff.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking that for each trip counted as served, its pickup node and dropoff node occur exactly once, on the same route, with the pickup index preceding the dropoff index, and that recompute_schedule_metrics reports pairing_violations == 0.

items.requirement: A passenger's request set (all of that passenger's trips) is only counted as served if every trip in the set is served; if any trip in the set is left unserved, none of that passenger's trips count as served.
items.source_quote: A request set counts as served only when every trip in that passenger's set is served; otherwise all trips in that set are unserved.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by grouping trips by passenger_id per requests.json, confirming that the served/unserved status recomputed by recompute_schedule_metrics is uniform within each passenger's trip set, and that served_trip_count plus unserved_trip_count equals the total flattened trip count.

items.requirement: Every served trip's dropoff arrival_time falls within [expected_arrival_time - time_window_width, expected_arrival_time], and its pickup arrival_time falls within [expected_arrival_time - time_window_width - direct_travel_time, expected_arrival_time - direct_travel_time], where direct_travel_time is the matrix entry from the pickup node to the dropoff node.
items.source_quote: Dropoff time window: `expected_arrival_time - time_window_width <= arrival_time <= expected_arrival_time`.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by recomputing each served trip's pickup and dropoff arrival_time from the submitted node sequences and confirming both fall within their respective windows, i.e. recompute_schedule_metrics reports time_window_violations == 0.

items.requirement: No route traverses an arc with a negative entry in t_matrix.csv.
items.source_quote: Routes must not use negative travel-time arcs.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by looking up every consecutive node pair used in each route's node_sequence against t_matrix.csv and confirming none of the values are negative, i.e. recompute_schedule_metrics reports invalid_arc_violations == 0.

items.requirement: At every visited pickup or dropoff node, the computed departure_time is at least arrival_time plus the applicable service time (pickup_service_time or dropoff_service_time).
items.verification: A grader can verify this by recomputing arrival_time and departure_time at each stop from the node sequence and confirming departure_time >= arrival_time + service_time for every stop, as enforced when validate_routes_for_schedule runs in test_route_feasibility.

items.requirement: The plan serves at least 95% of the trip count achieved by the reference solver's solution (submitted served_trip_count >= ceil(0.95 * reference served_trip_count)).
items.source_quote: Maximize the number of served trips; higher is better.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by computing the submitted schedule's served_trip_count via recompute_schedule_metrics and confirming it is at least ceil(reference_served * 0.95), where reference_served comes from solve_reference_report, matching the REFERENCE_SERVED_TRIP_RATIO check in test_reference_quality.

items.requirement: Vehicles that are not used to serve any trips are omitted from the routes list rather than included with an empty or depot-only route.
items.verification: A grader can verify this by checking that every route entry in the report's routes list has a node_sequence containing at least one pickup or dropoff node beyond the start/end depot nodes.
items.notes: Not independently enforced by a dedicated verifier assertion; a degenerate depot-to-depot route would not itself cause other tests to fail as long as it is otherwise feasible.
